evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.8.4: iī, quī potiuntur rērum
Cic. Rosc. Am. 70: cīvitās Athēniēnsium, dum ea rērum potīta est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rērum potīrī is to hold power in the state (Lewis & Short); Cicero’s phrase for the men in power in his day.

terms.gloss: the state; public affairs and their management
terms.grammar: noun, fifth declension, with an adjective
terms.comment: Traupman’s and Morgan–Owens’s first word for government; classically the commonwealth itself rather than the men who govern it.
Properly the offices, then the men who hold them.

terms.gloss: governing, the steering of a state

terms.comment: Post-Augustan, above all in Tacitus; not in Cicero or Caesar.

phrases.latin: ōtium nōbīs exoptandum est, quod iī, quī potiuntur rērum, praestātūrī videntur
phrases.english: we must hope for the peace and quiet that those in power seem ready to guarantee

sources: Lewis & Short: potior · Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: publicus · Lewis & Short: magistratus · Lewis & Short: gubernatio · Lewis & Short: regimen
